summary: Step 3 re-reads step 2's alleles with neither an aligner (a tool that decides where a read belongs on the genome) nor a variant caller (a tool that decides what a read implies about a genotype) in the loop: it counts, directly in the raw read bytes, how often the 31-letter sequence around each allele matches the reference spelling versus the alternate spelling. One copy of an allele shows up in about half the covering reads, two copies in nearly all, zero in a handful from sequencing noise — so multiplicity can be read off a count without ever modelling alignment. It typed 164,044 alleles (step 2's 75,733 plus 88,754 ClinVar pathogenic/likely-pathogenic alleles plus 20,000 calibration markers), fit a negative-binomial model to 1,876,842,047 read-window counts (variance-to-mean ratio 2.91, three times more dispersed than a naive Poisson model would assume), and measured copy number over 1,430 regions with no aligner at all — correctly recovering the proband's single X chromosome (median dosage 0.95 against 2.00 on autosomes) without being told the proband is male. Of six pre-registered claims, four were refuted and two supported; three data-processing bugs were caught mid-run by disbelieving a suspicious figure rather than by pre-built tests.
why: Every conclusion in step 2 passed through an aligner and a caller, both of which are models with assumptions about where a read belongs and what a haplotype looks like. If those assumptions are wrong in a specific gene, step 2's calls would be wrong in a way no re-reading of the same aligned data could catch — only an instrument with no aligner or caller in it can independently corroborate them. This mattered concretely: step 2 found 1,199 alleles the vendor's own callset never reported, and six of the ten target genes reached a biallelic candidate only through those alleles. Without an independent check, there is no way to know whether those 1,199 alleles are real or an artefact of the read-recovery pipeline — and the entire compound-heterozygous case for those six genes would rest on an unverified count.
verdict: H024 (every step-2 heterozygous call in a reachable target gene is confirmed) is refuted: 453 of 518 are, not all. H025 (a ClinVar pathogenic/likely-pathogenic allele is present at heterozygous multiplicity) is supported, but weakly: one allele is genuinely present, four others sit at alternate fractions of 0.06–0.09 — a tenth of a real heterozygote — and are flagged as a probable artefact of an error-rate estimate that is too tight. H026 (no target exon falls below the copy-number null band) is refuted: BRD4 exon 7 does, at 0.85. H027 (≥ 80% of the 1,199 vendor-unreported alleles are confirmed) is refuted — only 27–43% are, against 91–97% of vendor-reported alleles confirmed by the same instrument in the same run, meaning roughly two-thirds of those 1,199 alleles cannot be independently corroborated and every step-2 biallelic count resting on them is now known to be an upper bound. H028 (both lead alleles sit at one-copy multiplicity) is supported at posterior 1.0, unanimous across all three probes per allele — explicitly a dosage statement, not phase, and not evidence the two alleles are in trans. H029 (unreachable genes yield no confident genotype) is refuted: they yield 215 confident calls anyway.

inherits.what: The 75,733 step-2 alleles are exactly what this step sets out to corroborate or refute with an independent instrument, and the gene reachability flags from step 2's bait-density and MAPQ analysis (which genes the short-read aligner could place reads in at all) fix which genes this step is even allowed to report a confident genotype for.

hands_to.what: Step 4's genome-wide likelihood-ranking gets a measured, per-allele-origin error rate instead of a caveat: ~1 in 3 vendor-unreported alleles corroborated, ~19 in 20 vendor-reported ones, and a reachability flag per gene. It also hands forward `results.it2_kmer_pairs` — step 2's biallelic gene counts recounted using only k-mer-confirmed calls — and the dosage-only finding on the lead pair (both alleles at one copy each), which step 6's fusion has to weigh without ever treating it as phase evidence.

figures.name: mapq-profile.png
figures.reads: Grouped bars per tier (core, mechanism-term, net, decoy) on a log y-axis: the median gene's fraction of reads at mapping quality 0 (aligner could not place them confidently) versus the worst gene's fraction, in that tier.
figures.means: The reachability gate's own evidence: computed before any genotype model was fit, this shows the feared MAPQ-0 pile-up mostly did not happen, which is why the reachability rule could be stated up front rather than discovered as a limitation after the fact.

figures.name: probe-design.png
figures.reads: Horizontal stacked bars by allele origin (step-2 caller, ClinVar, calibration), green segment = alleles that got all three reference/alternate probe pairs, red segment = alleles with fewer or none.
figures.means: Evidence for the probe-design gate: 95,372 of 164,044 alleles were fully probed and 15,525 got none, all explicitly listed rather than silently dropped — the basis for trusting that a subsequent 'no-call' means insufficient probe coverage, not a hidden failure.

figures.name: calibration.png
figures.reads: Horizontal bar chart, log x-axis, of the negative-binomial fit's parameters: per-copy coverage from the alternate side and the reference side, the variance-to-mean ratio, dispersion, and the minimum count needed to call an allele 'present', with a dashed line at Poisson = 1.
figures.means: The variance-to-mean ratio of 2.91 sits far above the Poisson line, which is the justification for fitting a negative-binomial (over-dispersed) model rather than a simpler Poisson one — a Poisson model would have been three times too confident in every genotype call. The two per-copy coverage estimates differing by 5.6% is disclosed as reference bias, not repaired.

figures.name: confirmation.png
figures.reads: Grouped bars, target genes versus decoy genes, split by whether the allele set is vendor-reported or vendor-unreported, showing the fraction confirmed by the k-mer genotype instrument, with a dashed line at the H027 80% threshold and counts (confirmed/total) on each bar.
figures.means: The step's headline evidence: vendor-reported alleles confirm at 91–97% across all tiers (the instrument works), but vendor-unreported alleles confirm at only 27–43% — far under the 80% H027 needed — meaning about two-thirds of the 1,199 alleles the vendor callset missed cannot be independently corroborated, and every step-2 biallelic-candidate count built on them is an upper bound, not a confirmed count.

figures.name: calls-by-tier.png
figures.reads: Stacked bars per tier, segments for het, hom-alt, hom-ref and no-call allele counts.
figures.means: Shows a no-call is drawn as its own bar rather than hidden as a gap: 73,067 of the 164,044 typed alleles landed as no-call, and the distribution across het/hom-alt/hom-ref by tier is the raw material the confirmation and calibration figures are built from.

figures.name: reachability.png
figures.reads: Bar chart of the fraction of alleles called confidently, one bar per reachability category (reachable, or excluded for a named reason — sparse bait and/or aligner refused), colour green for reachable and red for excluded, with gene counts labelled on each bar.
figures.means: Evidence for H029's refutation: genes the reachability gate excluded still yield 215 confident calls, so 'excluded' cannot be read as 'silent' — the gate is a caution about coverage, not a guarantee that nothing can be said about those genes.

figures.name: copy-number.png
figures.reads: Bar chart of median copy number per tier (core, mechanism-term, net, decoy, and — implicitly — chromosome X), with a shaded null band measured from the decoys, a dashed line at the band's lower edge, a reference line at diploid = 2.0, and 'below band' region counts labelled per bar.
figures.means: The step's strongest validation: the null band [1.028, 2.823] is measured from this sample's own decoys rather than imported from a paper, autosomal tiers sit at median 2.00 inside it, and chromosome X reads at 0.95 — half the autosomal dosage — without the model ever being told the proband is male. One region, BRD4 exon 7 at 0.85, falls below the band, which is H026's refutation.

figures.name: index.html
figures.reads: Interactive contact sheet combining all seven static figures (mapq-profile, probe-design, calibration, confirmation, calls-by-tier, reachability, copy-number) with hover tooltips.
figures.means: Same evidence as the seven figures, in a form that lets a reader inspect exact per-bar values rather than reading them off a static image.
